title: ExAnte: A Benchmark for Ex-Ante Inference in Large Language Models
problem: Post-cutoff knowledge leakage in ex-ante inference
method: Four tasks plus leakage-rate and quality metrics
data: Stock prediction; QA; Wikipedia event generation; scientific publication generation
reported_result: Authors report frequent temporal-constraint violations across tasks
reported_limit_or_scope: Benchmark scope does not itself establish actor-specific historical accessibility
differentiation_risk: High: directly covers cutoff leakage measurement

title: Can Prompts Rewind Time for LLMs? Evaluating the Effectiveness of Prompted Knowledge Cutoffs
problem: Whether prompts can simulate an earlier knowledge cutoff
method: Two meta-prompts across direct fact, semantic shift and causal/counterfactual subsets
data: Three released evaluation subsets; author repository records a post-publication quality cleanup
reported_result: Prompted forgetting is stronger for direct facts and semantic shifts than for causally related counterfactual knowledge
reported_limit_or_scope: Repository states low-quality samples were removed; exact dataset version must be frozen
differentiation_risk: High: establishes a stronger prompt baseline and exposes indirect hindsight leakage

title: EvolveBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Assessing Temporal Awareness in LLMs on Evolving Knowledge
problem: Temporal awareness under evolving and externally supplied knowledge
method: Five dimensions: cognition, awareness, trustworthiness, understanding and reasoning
reported_result: GPT-4o average EM 79.36 and Llama3.1-70B 72.47; all models still struggle with temporally misaligned context
reported_limit_or_scope: Modern evolving-fact setting does not supply historical archive accessibility evidence
differentiation_risk: Medium-high: overlaps temporal conflict evaluation but not historical epistemic reachability

title: Can LLMs Be Constrained to the Past? Improving Knowledge Cutoff through Recall-Based Prompting
problem: Indirect post-cutoff leakage and robustness across cutoffs
data: Three existing benchmarks plus Multi-cutoff Historical Event Benchmark (MHEB)
reported_result: Authors report SR-to-QR consistently best and especially strong gains on counterfactual questions
reported_limit_or_scope: Self-recalled facts are not independent evidence of temporal admissibility

title: Can Language Models Represent the Past without Anachronism?
method: Period-prose prompting; fine-tuning; automated and human discrimination
data: Historical prose simulation corpus and evaluator comparisons
reported_result: Prompting did not yield period-consistent text; fine-tuned outputs fooled an automated judge but remained distinguishable to humans
reported_limit_or_scope: Primarily evaluates prose simulation and style rather than cutoff-constrained factual QA
differentiation_risk: High for construct validity: stylistic plausibility cannot stand in for historical validity

title: Teaching Large Language Models When Not to Know: Learning Temporal Critique for Ex-Ante Reasoning
problem: Cutoff-relative temporal admissibility of candidate answers
method: Prompt-position analysis plus Temporal Critique Fine-Tuning (TCFT)
data: Cutoff-conditioned query-response critique data; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and 14B-Instruct
reported_result: Authors report average leakage reductions of 41.89 and 37.79 percentage points over prompting/SFT baselines
reported_limit_or_scope: Cross-domain transfer, label provenance and generator transfer require separate checking
differentiation_risk: Very high: directly adjacent to proposition-level temporal verification

title: HistoRAG: Embedding Historical Methodology in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Through Critical Technical Practice
problem: Temporal and lexical skew in historical retrieval
method: Separated retrieval/generation; temporal windowing; keyword plus semantic retrieval; contestable relevance filtering
reported_result: Era-specific terminology retrieved zero 1950s chunks in one probe; vector similarity and LLM relevance correlated weakly at Spearman rho 0.275
reported_limit_or_scope: Temporal windowing balances periods but does not by itself enforce proposition-level cutoff admissibility
differentiation_risk: High for M2: simple historical windowing is already occupied

title: Time Sensitive Knowledge Editing through Efficient Finetuning
problem: Updating obsolete facts and injecting new facts
method: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning compared with locate-and-edit methods; layer probing
data: Temporal knowledge-editing dataset with updates and injections plus multi-hop QA
reported_result: Authors report PEFT outperforms locate-and-edit methods for time-sensitive edits
reported_limit_or_scope: Forward updating to newer facts is not evidence that a model can rewind to arbitrary historical cutoffs
differentiation_risk: Medium: adjacent parameter route but objective direction differs
